Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 07/31/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Ortiz presents for routine follow-up. She reports no new complaints today. She denies any recent falls or injuries.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Neurological exam is intact with no focal deficits. Musculoskeletal exam shows no swelling or deformity.

Assessment:
Ms. Ortiz is an elderly female with stable health status. No new issues identified during today's visit.

Plan:
Continue current health maintenance and monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up as needed or for routine care.

Hospital Admission History and Physical
Date: 09/17/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85-year-old female

Chief Complaint:
Admitted 09/17/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 10/10 despite IV analgesia.

History of Present Illness:
Ms. Ortiz presents with severe back pain that has necessitated hospital admission. The pain is described as constant and severe, rated 10 out of 10 on the numeric rating scale despite intravenous analgesic administration.

Past Medical History:
Includes hypertension, osteoarthritis, and mild chronic kidney disease.

Physical Examination:
Vital signs are stable. On examination, there is tenderness over the lumbar spine region without visible deformity or swelling. Neurological examination reveals no focal deficits; motor strength and sensation are intact in all extremities.

Assessment:
Severe back pain requiring inpatient management. No neurological compromise noted.

Plan:
Continue pain management with close monitoring. Further diagnostic evaluation to determine underlying cause will be pursued. Supportive care and consultation with relevant specialties as needed.

notes.title: Radiology Report
notes.author: Radiologist
notes.text:
Radiology Report
Date: 09/10/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/10/2026: chronic-appearing L1 compression deformity without bone marrow edema.

No acute fractures or bone marrow edema are identified. The remainder of the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae appear unremarkable. No abnormal paraspinal soft tissue masses or fluid collections are seen.

Impression:
Chronic-appearing L1 compression deformity without bone marrow edema. No evidence of acute fracture or other acute pathology.

notes.title: Spine Intervention Consultation
notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/21/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 09/01/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 3 weeks before this visit. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Assessment:
The patient has a vertebral compression fracture corresponding to the site of pain. There are no signs of systemic infection or discitis.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. The patient will be monitored and managed accordingly.
